# Compliance matrix

Every requirement of the study, the document that will show compliance, the method behind it and the state of the evidence today. Generated from the model: the document register and the change classification live in `model/compliance.yaml`.

## Change classification

**Status**: OPEN — **proposed**: MAJOR

- **Basis**: EASA Part 21 Subpart D. The classification is made by the design organisation under 21.A.263(c)(1); a minor change is approved under 21.A.95, a major change under 21.A.97.
- **Approval route**: 21.A.97 (major change), unless the design organisation concludes a minor change under its own procedure and approves it under 21.A.95.
- **Privileges**: 21.A.263(c)(1) classification, 21.A.263(c)(2) approval of minor changes, 21.A.263(c)(5) and (8) major change approval under privileges where the terms of approval allow it.

| Criterion | Appreciable effect | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weight and balance | YES | The installation adds up to 60 kg including the payload, forward of the centre of gravity reference and outside the certified range until the weight and balance report is updated. |
| Structural strength | YES | New fittings transfer the payload loads into the platform primary structure at four hard points, with a fitting factor of 1.15. |
| Electrical system | YES | A new protected 20 A circuit and a new load enter the platform distribution and its electrical load analysis. |
| Avionics and data interfaces | YES | ARINC 429 control and a digital video link are added to the mission system interface panel. |
| Environmental protection | YES | The installation changes the lightning, static and HIRF paths, and adds an external emissive and receiving unit. |
| Operating limitations and flight manual | YES | Loading information changes, and the flight manual supplement has to record any operating limitation that follows. |
| Instructions for continued airworthiness | YES | New scheduled inspections, wear items and a payload replacement procedure enter the maintenance programme. |
| Flight characteristics | OPEN | Drag, mass distribution and any effect on the handling qualities are not assessed in this study; the assessment belongs to the platform. |
| Safety assessment | OPEN | No ARP4761A assessment is performed in this study. It is the first activity to schedule if the classification is confirmed. |

**Open items**

- The platform change classification procedure and the terms of approval.
- The appreciable effect assessment on flight characteristics and on the electrical system.
- The safety assessment, which this study does not perform.

## Instructions for continued airworthiness

The outline of the instructions for continued airworthiness is in `docs/ica.md`; it covers the installation, the payload replacement procedure, the scheduled inspections, the wear items and the parts list. Intervals and wear limits come with the platform maintenance programme and are still open.
